title: Crowback and passing for white; the Memphis excursion story
summary: Vincent describes Crowback, who tried to pass as white, and a story of a fair-skinned man on a Chicago-to-Memphis excursion exposed when he said he was colored.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Ask him who Crowback worked with. Crowback? Yeah, Crowback.
Say, who did Crowback work with? The Dixon band. Yeah, he's from downtown Cleveland, you know.
Yeah, he worked with us for a while. But not a real member, you know.

You know Crowback, huh? No. Crowback is the one who tried to be white on the side, you know. And he figured if he'd get to go out there, white boy, and he'd talk just like a white boy, you know. Hey, you guys, you know what I'm singing this? Say, because you guys give me a shot, damn pen with them guys up there, you know. And he wouldn't say he was a white boy, you know, but he was a father, he tried to pass my wife, you know. The real big guy, he never did try. No. The real big guy go down and the white boy starts to fight. They say, I'm a cut it, boy. I'm a cut it, boy. And when the cut it, boy starts to fight, they say, I'm a white boy. I'm a white boy. But he couldn't get rid of it, no kind of way. I said, Dick, you know, I have to tell you about a pretty excursion from Chicago to Memphis. And the fellow we had, they had the booster club. But the fellow, he looked like a white guy, you see. Well, some guys got to fighting in the place, and the police was packing down. So the police were coming to hooking him, got Doc's head around there, you see. So Charlie, his name was Charlie, Charlie something, I forget his last name. But anyhow, he looked like a white man. But when he got to talking, see, he messed himself up. He said, you Polish mums, he said, every time the colored people started giving him something around here, he said, you all better come in and break it up. He said, now look what a damn Charlie broke up. Well, he talked that nice, because it's all these whites, you know. He said, well, you know, I said, we're trying to help you, see. We thought maybe we'd stop the fight and things, so and so and so. He said, oh yeah, I know. He said, we colored people, this can't have no funny. And he said, you colored? He said, yeah.
He hit him up. He got a student there going in.
If he would have never said that, he would have never went with me.
He could talk like a white man.

Yeah, he talk like him, see. Like, did he, did he, did he, did he, did he, did he. He said, oh no, I know, he said, we colored people, can't give him. He said, you colored? He said, yeah, boy, that was it. Henry, that was the name, Henry Robert. No, Robert Henry, Robert Henry. Robert Henry. Robert Henry. And he beat him up.
Yeah. Did you ever know that fella called Robert Henry used to run the booster discussion?
Robert Henry. Robert Henry. Memphis. From Memphis. I made more money than I had to make more money one night. You told me about that. That's right. Do you remember Bobby?
